questions: No additional substantive interpretation of the exact target clause is supported beyond the prior activity-specific and entity-wide readings. Does “acting as a Transfer Agent” concern these funds or any concurrent activity of the LC?

Does the full sentence intend the listed conditions collectively to suffice for Q1 applicability? “Only when” alone establishes a necessary condition, and the proposed Boolean does not decide legal sufficiency.

Does “In such cases” extend Schedule 11 expectations to every transfer-agent exclusion, or only to the immediately preceding money category? Q3 confirms Schedule 11 expectations in specified other circumstances but does not resolve that reference.

What incorporated definitions and missing dependency govern the external classifications? Q2’s timing and unknown-receipt qualifications should not become additional Q1 conditions without supporting authority.

citations.quote: only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent
Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?

readings.distinction: The defensible rivals concern acting in the particular handling and acting anywhere concurrently. Both attach “not” to “acting as a Transfer Agent” and treat “only when” as restricting the coordinated application statement. Q1’s activity-specific question favors the first reading. This retains an existing interpretation rather than claiming a newly discovered alternative; reversing the negation or restricting it to AE-held money lacks adequate textual support.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent.

readings.distinction: This existing rival takes the LC itself as the scope of acting status. Concurrent unrelated transfer-agent work therefore defeats the antecedent for otherwise qualifying handling. “Such LC” supports retaining the possibility, although Q1’s focus on activities in a particular capacity weighs against it. The source does not conclusively settle the scope.
questions: What supplied fact distinguishes any concurrent transfer-agent work from transfer-agent handling of these funds? Reusing transfer_agent with a different index would conceal the disagreement rather than encode it.
What time or period defines concurrent acting? The vocabulary supplies neither a time index nor an activity aggregation predicate.

vocabulary_concerns: transfer_agent has no funds, activity or time index. The activity-specific expression is conditional on an explicit input convention; the fixed vocabulary cannot independently represent and compare both scopes.
ra13_context combines actor identity and handling in the course of RA13. It cannot separately test LC and AE handling or their relationship while keeping the express qualification focused on the LC.

scheme_money depends on incorporated definitions not supplied here. Q3’s account ownership, REIT-property and SPV circumstances inform classification but cannot be separately represented by these facts.
An antecedent Boolean does not represent the necessary-versus-sufficient force of “only when” as a rule about legal applicability.
No supplied fact represents Schedule 11 expectations, their modality, their satisfaction or the referent of “In such cases”. A false antecedent is not a whole-law exemption.
Q2’s general timing rule, unknown-receipt exception and contrary-evidence qualification are not expressible with these inputs. Unknown classifications must remain unknown.
